# Contributing

Sinner's Workshop is a **free, non-commercial, fan-made** project, not affiliated with Project Moon. There are no ads, donations or paid features. Everyone taking part follows the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## How to suggest or report

- **Discord** (ideas, questions, custom kits): https://discord.gg/hZgMnDN5K
- **GitHub issues**: https://github.com/pixelenjoyer57-droid/limbus-calculator/issues/new/choose (bug report, suggestion, rights holder request)
- **Security problems:** privately, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Terms

1. If you post suggestions, bug reports or custom kits on Discord or GitHub, you allow the maintainers to use, adapt and include them in the app and its data without payment. You keep the rights to your own work. We name you in public, for example in the changelog, only if you say yes. Otherwise it says "community suggestion". We keep only your display name, the channel and the date. Giving a name is optional. We may copy suggestions, bug reports and custom kits you post on Discord or GitHub into our private notes. We may read them with third-party AI tools to help plan the work. We keep your name while we consider the idea. We delete it from our notes on request. Your original post stays under Discord's or GitHub's own rules. To ask us to name you, or to delete your name, message a Discord moderator or comment on your GitHub issue. Please leave personal details out of public comments.
2. Only share what you made or may share. No leaks, unreleased or datamined content, ripped game art or audio, or other people's private information.
3. **Code** contributions (pull requests) are licensed under the MIT license ([LICENSE](../LICENSE)). You confirm you have the right to submit them. You are responsible for AI-assisted code too, and you confirm you may submit it.
4. **Game-data** changes (`public/gamedata/`) are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 ([LICENSE-DATA.md](../LICENSE-DATA.md)). The data files are generated by `scripts/gamedata/`; change the importer where possible.
5. Project Moon's material stays Project Moon's. Rights holders: use the "Rights holder request" issue form or contact a Discord moderator.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # local dev server
npm test           # engine and formula tests (vitest)
npm run build      # type-check and build to dist/
```

Stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite, zustand + immer for state, zod for validating saved and imported data, and a Web Worker for simulations. Navigation uses the URL hash, so the build works from any sub-folder.

```
src/engine/    combat engine (formulas, statuses, effects, clashes, turns, calculator, batch runs); no UI code
src/data/      content schema, defaults and templates, import and migration
src/gamedata/  loading, picking and copying the in-game data
src/store/     workspace (autosave, undo), session ("where was I"), settings, toasts
src/features/  screens: home, library (builder), team, calc, sim, data, help, about
src/ui/        accessible components (number steppers, sections, dialogs, tips)
src/app/, src/lib/  app shell, router, file and worker helpers
scripts/       game-data importer (reads the Limbus Company Wiki)
tests/         vitest suites
```

### Game data

The files in `public/gamedata/` are **generated**, with one item per line so diffs stay readable. Don't edit them by hand; refresh them from the wiki instead:

- `npm run gamedata` fetches from the wiki and keeps a local cache in `.cache/wiki`.
- `npm run gamedata -- --offline` reuses the cache.
- `npm run gamedata -- --report <file>` lists the most common effect sentences that aren't simulated yet.

### Pull requests

1. Branch from `main` and keep each pull request to one change.
2. Before opening it, run `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`, `npx vitest run` and `npm run build`. If the UI changed, try it on a phone-sized screen too.
3. The `test-and-build` check must pass. Pull requests are squash-merged.

Every merge to `main` is tested and deployed to GitHub Pages automatically (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`).
